answer: Copper-cut reachability weighting. Each agent’s vote weight is capped by the number of distinct ingress paths its traffic traverses, measured as edge-disjoint routes through the relay graph. A zephyr of new identities sharing one upstream link collapses to a single path, so their combined influence stays at one unit regardless of headcount. To gain weight, an attacker must provision genuinely separate network positions with independent peering and latency profiles, paying recurring transit and onyx-grade monitoring costs per identity rather than a one-time registration fee.
